svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
44 × 52 holes · cut to 111.8 × 132.1 mm · 26 cuts · 26 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Every physical control, MIDI, the relay and the LEDs.
C12 100nF — across the battery divider, at the ADC pin
D4 1N5817 — band towards VSYS, the right-hand lead
Q1 BC337 — flat face towards you, pins down: emitter, base, collector. That
is the usual BC337 order; check the bag before soldering
R16 1k — LED 1, and the three beside it LED 2 to LED 4, each 1 kΩ
R21 100k — base to the emitter, so the relay stays off while the Pico boots
R22 330k — battery sense, the bottom resistor, to ground
R23 100k — adapter-present sense, the bottom resistor
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
D3 → Core breakout, JST-XH 4-way (B4B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 Pico TX (GP0) → Pi
RXD, pin 10 · 3 Pico RX (GP1) ← Pi TXD, pin 8 · 4 +5 V hold
C1 → Bypass relay, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 COIL − · 2 — · 3 +5 V
No ground: the coil’s low side is switched on the control board, so no
C2 → MIDI in, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 MIDI RX · 3 3V3
C4 → Footswitches ×3 + LEDs ×4, JST-XH 8-way (B8B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 FS1 · 3
FS2 · 4 FS3 · 5 LED1 · 6 LED2 · 7 LED3 · 8 LED4
C5 → Encoder + back, JST-XH 6-way (B6B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 ENC A · 3 ENC B · 4
P4 → 9 V power, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 VBAT · 2 VDC · 3 —
No ground: a high-value resistor at the power end of each wire; the
GND reaches the root through D3 only (Core breakout).
GP0 and GP1 are the link, which the firmware already uses. Every other GPIO
on this drawing is a proposal. The firmware has not claimed those pins, so
treat the labels as a suggestion for the first build.
The diode is why the Pico keeps running when the Pi reboots. Its 5 V is the
header’s last pin, which is the Pi’s pin 4, and the band faces VSYS. VBUS,
the pin beside it, is left open.
The coil’s low side is switched here, so the cable to the relay carries no
ground. The 100 kΩ holds the transistor off until something explicitly turns
the relay on. The flyback diode is on the relay board.
The USB console lead and the Debug Probe plug into the Pico’s own sockets.
They are not headers on this board.
The expression jack is not drawn. Its plug is the map’s C6, and its filter
would sit at one of the remaining ADC pins.
Cut every strip between the Pico’s two rows, at the marked hole, and the
strips under the series resistors. The four ground rows are joined inside
the Pico, so a cut on a ground row does not break the ground.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
